0.long_answer: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) due to 3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase deficiency results from a defect in the enzyme responsible for converting delta-5 steroids (such as pregnenolone and 17α-hydroxypregnenolone) into their corresponding delta-4 steroids. This enzymatic block leads to the accumulation of 17α-hydroxypregnenolone and other precursors. Unlike the more common 21-hydroxylase deficiency, which typically causes virilization primarily in females, 3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase deficiency can result in ambiguous genitalia in both individuals with XX and XY chromosomal patterns. The elevated 17α-hydroxypregnenolone level serves as a key biochemical marker for this form of CAH.
